_help.about: [NOT WIRED YET — design §ET.9] The NPC maker: character creation recycled to randomize folk. Each figure rolls a kind, a cloak style and colours, proportions and a set of parts, then bakes to its own sprite sheets (crawler.json sprites, §ET.8). First guesses by Claude (chat), 6 Oct; the designer owns them. Part names are placeholders until the parts are made.
_help.kinds: human: hood down, hair and face show (new in §ET.9). beast: a §EO/§EQ head under a cowl, no hair or face parts. The number is the share of folk who roll each.
_help.cloak: styles: the shared wardrobe; every kind draws from it. Cloak and hem colours, and the player's reserved indigo with the rust hem, stay in cloaks.json (colors, avoid).
_help.proportions: PSO-style sliders: each is a range the roll picks within; 1.0 is the rig as built.
_help.hair_colors: Fire Emblem-style. A figure rolls natural or wild by weight (wild is the spice), then a colour from that list. sRGB hex.
_help.parts: Preset parts per slot, mixed and matched. count: how many to make first. chance: the share of humans who roll one (1 means always). Under §EH, jewellery is bone, shell, stone or wood. glasses: there is no glass (retired 5 Oct); snow-goggle slits of bone or wood fit the snow ruins, or Mike drops the slot (§ET.9). §EH is superseded by §FL.1 (7 Oct: metal and glass are allowed again); the parts stay as they are until Mike says. At 270 lines (§ES) earrings and nose rings are a pixel or two even close: they read up close and in the portrait.
_help.portrait: The HUD portrait (§ET.9): a crop of the figure's own baked sprite, front angle, eye-level row. No separate art. Whose face it shows is open (§ET.10 call 9).
